observations.text: Reviewed payExec native send regression tests in 0e9a3abe and 4deb9d71 assert wrong transactionHash receipt rejection, preserved submitted hash and no resend; 0e9a3abe additionally covers unsupported receipt status and JSON-array transaction fields. This supports PN-01 disposition, not a new issue. Tests inspected, not run.

Reviewed txGuard malformed ERC20 boolean regression block in #305 blob and complete sibling diff showing its absence from #303. Canonical true, false, empty return and generic eth_call behavior are distinguished. Tests inspected, not run.

duplicateAttemptJournal and walletJournal sources explicitly retain attempts, require explicit clearing, and block invoice repeats across changed calldata/accounts. They reinforce the known missing route recovery wiring impact; no new issue claimed.

A Pay route regression test ALREADY exists: Pay.test.tsx 647–663 performs a rejected send, verifies a duplicate block, confirms clearing through the real rendered route and verifies a second wallet request. git rev-parse on affected #300 commit confirms the file is blob 7ef3db70; full render helper inspection shows renderApp mounts App with ServicesContext and no WalletAttempts substitution. This corrects the claim that Pay has no route-level clearing coverage. The affected production WalletAttempts requires a wallet prop, while inspected Pay call sites still omit it, so the existing test expectation is inconsistent with that branch source. Static inspection supports expecting the test to expose BROWSER-01 when run; no execution or observed test failure is claimed. Further pre-existing/account-change/chain-change regression coverage can still be extended.
